title: Generators of a regular principal ideal sheaf are associated
statement: Let C be a small site with topology J and O a commutative ring sheaf. Let I be an ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal] and t,a global sections of O. Suppose I(U) is the principal ideal generated by t(U) for every U, multiplication by t(U) is injective on O(U), and the singleton a(U) generates the ideal module on every slice in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators]. There is a rank-one module-sheaf automorphism c of O with scalar(t)=c.hom followed by scalar(a), where the scalar endomorphisms are those of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. This also holds for empty sites and zero rings.

source.place: Lemma derived-completion-koszul (0A0E), rank-one scalar comparison; literature/blueprint/latest/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-thm-sf-pf-adic/sk-thm-sf-pf-adic-open.proof.md, reduction paragraph.

proof.text: Construct maps alpha,tau:O -> I by multiplying by a,t respectively. The singleton generator hypothesis puts a in I; the stated principal-ideal formula puts t in I. Regularity makes tau injective, and the principal-ideal formula makes it surjective on every object. Thus tau is an isomorphism.

Alpha is epic: on a slice all specified generating sections coincide with the section alpha(1), as sections on a slice are determined at its terminal object. The generating free-module epimorphism therefore factors through alpha on that slice. Evaluate cancellation at the slice terminal object to deduce cancellation globally.

The epic endomorphism alpha followed by tau inverse is invertible. Indeed the underlying abelian-sheaf map is epic since forgetting module structure preserves colimits. Local surjectivity lifts 1 on a covering sieve. Every rank-one linear endomorphism is multiplication by its value on 1; a lift of 1 makes this value a unit locally. It is thus locally injective and globally injective by separatedness. Mono and epi imply isomorphism in the abelian module-sheaf category.
Consequently alpha is invertible. Set c=tau followed by alpha inverse. Cancel alpha inverse with alpha after the ideal inclusion to obtain the claimed equation.

lean.statement:
theorem ringed_regular_generator_association
    (I : RingedSiteIdeal O) (t a : (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (ht : ∀ U : C, I.sections U = Ideal.span {t.val (op U)})
    (hreg : ∀ U : C, Function.Injective
      (fun x : O.obj.obj (op U) ↦ @Mul.mul (O.obj.obj (op U)) inferInstance (t.val (op U)) x))
    (ha : ∀ U : C, IsRingedIdealGeneratingList O I.module I.inclusion U 1
      (fun _ ↦ a.val (op U))) :
    ∃ c : SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings O) ≅
        SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings O),
      ringedKoszulScalar O t = c.hom ≫ ringedKoszulScalar O a
